indicators.indicator: Cybersecurity policy is documented and maintained
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF items and CCM controls together cover establishing and reviewing the policy
indicators.weight_rationale: Policy underpins other controls, but a missing policy does not by itself expose a specific asset

indicators.indicator: Security responsibilities, including the division between the organization and the cloud provider, are defined
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF items are broader. The CCM controls specify the ownership of controls between provider and customer
indicators.weight_rationale: Unassigned responsibilities can leave critical controls unimplemented across several services

indicators.indicator: Cloud security risks are assessed and recorded
indicators.relationship_note: The indicator assesses whether a risk assessment exists and guides priorities, not its method
indicators.weight_rationale: Risk assessment guides priorities across the system, but its absence has an indirect, contained effect

indicators.indicator: Cloud providers and other suppliers are assessed and bound by security requirements
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF items cover requirements and due diligence, and the CCM controls specify agreement and assurance review
indicators.weight_rationale: Weak supplier assurance affects the services of that supplier and is contained to them

indicators.indicator: Systems, services and data are inventoried
indicators.relationship_note: One indicator combines the system, service and data inventories of the sources
indicators.weight_rationale: Several other controls depend on knowing which systems, services and data must be protected

indicators.indicator: Staff receive security awareness training
indicators.relationship_note: The items are equivalent in intent
indicators.weight_rationale: Awareness mainly supports other controls, and its absence limits their effectiveness

indicators.indicator: Users and services have unique identities and managed credentials
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify unique identities, credentials and identity inventory
indicators.weight_rationale: Shared or unmanaged identities weaken accountability and access control across critical services

indicators.indicator: Strong authentication protects access
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF item is broader. The CCM control specifies strong authentication
indicators.weight_rationale: A compromised account without strong authentication can give access to the whole system

indicators.indicator: Access follows least privilege, separation of duties and controlled privileged roles
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF item is broader. The CCM controls specify least privilege, separation of duties and privileged roles, which the indicator combines
indicators.weight_rationale: Excessive or privileged rights can extend a single compromise to the whole system, and other controls depend on them

indicators.indicator: Access is reviewed and revoked promptly
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF item is broader. The CCM controls specify access review and revocation
indicators.weight_rationale: Stale access creates a significant but contained exposure for the accounts concerned

indicators.indicator: Data at rest is encrypted
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(1)(a) names encryption as an example of an appropriate measure
indicators.weight_rationale: Unencrypted stored data can expose a critical data store

indicators.indicator: Data in transit is encrypted
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(1)(a) names encryption as an example of an appropriate measure
indicators.weight_rationale: Unencrypted transmission can expose critical data between services and users

indicators.indicator: Cryptographic keys are managed through their life cycle
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF items are broader, because the CSF has no key management subcategory. The CCM controls specify the key life cycle

csa_ccm_v4_1: CEK-01 (Encryption and Key Management Policy and Procedures)

indicators.weight_rationale: Key compromise or loss can expose or destroy all data protected by the keys, and other cryptographic controls depend on it

indicators.indicator: The organization controls its own encryption keys where the service allows it
indicators.relationship_note: The CSF item is broader. The CCM control specifies the customer key management capability
indicators.weight_rationale: Provider-held keys limit control over data, but the indicator applies only to services that offer customer-managed keys

indicators.indicator: Security-relevant events are logged and monitored
indicators.relationship_note: The items together cover logging scope, monitoring and the response to alerts
indicators.weight_rationale: Without logging and monitoring, attacks on critical assets can go undetected

indicators.indicator: Vulnerabilities are identified and remediated
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify identification and remediation scheduling
indicators.weight_rationale: Unremediated vulnerabilities can allow compromise of critical components

indicators.indicator: Configuration and changes are controlled
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify the change policy and the configuration baseline
indicators.weight_rationale: Insecure configuration or uncontrolled change can expose critical cloud resources

indicators.indicator: Networks and cloud resources are protected from unauthorized access
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify network security and segmentation
indicators.weight_rationale: Unrestricted network exposure can allow direct access to critical resources

indicators.indicator: Endpoints used to access the system are protected
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify endpoint management and malware protection
indicators.weight_rationale: A compromised endpoint has a significant but contained effect on the data and accounts it can reach

indicators.indicator: Security measures are tested regularly
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(1)(d) calls for a process for regularly testing the effectiveness of measures
indicators.weight_rationale: Testing mainly verifies other controls, and its absence delays the discovery of weaknesses

indicators.indicator: An incident response plan exists and is tested
indicators.relationship_note: The CCM controls specify the plan, its testing and notification
indicators.weight_rationale: Without a tested plan, an incident affecting a critical service is contained late

indicators.indicator: Backups are created, protected and tested
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(1)(c) refers to the ability to restore availability and access to personal data
indicators.weight_rationale: Without usable backups, data loss may be unrecoverable, and recovery depends on them

indicators.indicator: A business continuity and disaster recovery plan exists
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(1)(b) and (c) refer to resilience and restoration
indicators.weight_rationale: Continuity planning affects the speed of recovery of services but not the occurrence of incidents

indicators.indicator: Personal data processing is inventoried and mapped
indicators.relationship_note: The Privacy Framework and CCM items cover the inventory. Article 5(2) is partial, because it places accountability on the controller and does not itself prescribe an inventory
indicators.weight_rationale: Other privacy controls depend on knowing which personal data are processed, where and why

indicators.indicator: Purposes of processing are documented and communicated
indicators.relationship_note: Article 5(1)(a) and (b) set transparency and purpose limitation. The lawful bases for processing are set in a provision outside the selection and are not assessed

csa_ccm_v4_1: DSP-12 (Limitation of Purpose in Personal Data Processing)

indicators.weight_rationale: Processing without documented and communicated purposes affects all processing of the data concerned

indicators.indicator: Privacy responsibilities and legal requirements are assigned and understood
indicators.relationship_note: The Privacy Framework and CCM items cover responsibilities and requirements. Article 5(2) is partial, because it places accountability on the controller and does not itself assign privacy responsibilities
indicators.weight_rationale: Unassigned responsibilities reduce accountability across privacy controls, but the impact is indirect

indicators.indicator: Data protection is built into design and defaults
indicators.relationship_note: The indicator corresponds to data protection by design and by default in Article 25

csa_ccm_v4_1: DSP-07 (Data Protection by Design and Default)
DSP-08 (Data Privacy by Design and Default)

indicators.weight_rationale: Neglecting design and defaults creates a significant but contained exposure for the affected processing

indicators.indicator: A data protection impact assessment is carried out where required
indicators.relationship_note: Article 35 sets when an impact assessment is required, and the indicator assesses readiness to carry one out
indicators.weight_rationale: A missing assessment leaves high-risk processing unexamined, which is contained to that processing

indicators.indicator: Staff handling personal data are aware of their duties
indicators.relationship_note: Article 32(4) concerns processing on instructions, and the indicator also covers training

csa_ccm_v4_1: HRS-12 (Personal and Sensitive Data Awareness and Training)

indicators.weight_rationale: Awareness mainly supports other controls

indicators.indicator: Only necessary personal data are collected and processed
indicators.relationship_note: Article 5(1)(c) sets data minimisation, and Article 25(2) applies it by default

csa_ccm_v4_1: DSP-07 (Data Protection by Design and Default)

indicators.weight_rationale: Excess data enlarge the exposure of individuals in a breach and the impact of every other failure

indicators.indicator: Personal data are retained only as long as necessary and then deleted
indicators.relationship_note: Article 5(1)(e) sets storage limitation
indicators.weight_rationale: Data kept longer than necessary enlarge the exposure of a critical data store

indicators.indicator: Personal data are kept accurate, and inaccurate data are corrected or erased
indicators.relationship_note: Article 5(1)(d) sets accuracy and the correction or erasure of inaccurate data. The rights of individuals to rectification and erasure are set in other provisions outside the selection and are not assessed

csa_ccm_v4_1: DSP-11 (Personal Data Access, Reversal, Rectification and Deletion)

indicators.weight_rationale: Inaccurate data cause significant but contained harm

indicators.indicator: Personal data are pseudonymised or encrypted where appropriate
indicators.relationship_note: Articles 25(1) and 32(1)(a) name pseudonymisation, and Article 32(1)(a) names encryption
indicators.weight_rationale: Without pseudonymisation or encryption, a breach exposes personal data directly

indicators.indicator: Access to personal data is limited to those who need it
indicators.relationship_note: Article 25(2) supports limiting the accessibility of personal data by default, and Article 5(1)(f) addresses integrity and confidentiality. The role-based access restriction itself is supported mainly by the CCM controls
indicators.weight_rationale: Uncontrolled access can expose all personal data in the system

indicators.indicator: Personal data breaches can be detected, handled and communicated
indicators.relationship_note: The GDPR references cover only the security of processing against personal data breaches. The notification part is mapped to the Privacy Framework and the CCM only, because the GDPR notification provisions are outside the selected articles
indicators.weight_rationale: Late or missing handling and communication affect the individuals concerned after an incident, which is a contained impact
